title: Strict relative lifting after hypercover refinement for local acyclic fibrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ given by covering sieves: a sieve is a set of arrows into an object closed under precomposition, the maximal sieve covers, and covering sieves satisfy pullback stability and transitivity. No fibre products or subcanonicity are assumed. Use [def-weil-size-convention] for universes and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] for associated sheaves.

Write $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$. A hypercover $U_\bullet\to h_T$ is an augmented simplicial presheaf of sets whose terms are small coproducts of representables and whose augmented matching maps become epimorphisms after sheafification. The degree-zero matching presheaf is $h_T$; all higher matching presheaves, parametrizing compatible proper faces, are formed in presheaves. A refinement over $T$ means a morphism of augmented simplicial presheaves over $h_T$. A collection is dense if every hypercover over every $T$ admits a refinement by a member of that collection over the same $T$.

Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. A simplicial presheaf is a functor $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$, and $h_T$ is regarded as a discrete simplicial presheaf. Write $\Delta^n$ for the represented standard simplex, $\partial\Delta^n$ for its boundary (empty for $n=0$), and $\Lambda_i^n$ for the union of all faces except face $i$, where $n\ge1$ and $0\le i\le n$. An objectwise Kan simplicial presheaf takes values in simplicial sets with fillers for every horn. A map $f:F\to G$ is a local Kan fibration if every commutative square from $h_V\times\Lambda_i^n\to h_V\times\Delta^n$ to $f$ has fillers after restriction along every arrow in some covering sieve of $V$; the fillers need not agree for different arrows of that sieve. For objectwise Kan $F,G$, call $f$ a local weak equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on the associated sheaves of $\pi_0$ and, for each $V\in\mathcal C$, $x\in F(V)_0$ and $m\ge1$, on the associated sheaves on $\mathcal C/V$ of $\pi_m(F|_{\mathcal C/V},x)\to\pi_m(G|_{\mathcal C/V},f(x))$. The slice topology is induced by covering sieves.

Let $F,G$ be objectwise Kan simplicial presheaves and let $f:F\to G$ be both a local Kan fibration and a local weak equivalence. Let $U_\bullet\to h_T$ be any hypercover, let $i:K\hookrightarrow L$ be an inclusion of simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices (allowing $K=\varnothing$), and let $a:K\times U_\bullet\to F$ and $b:L\times U_\bullet\to G$ satisfy $f a=b(i\times1)$. Then there are a hypercover $V_\bullet\to h_T$, a refinement $v:V_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ over $h_T$, and a simplicial-presheaf map $\ell:L\times V_\bullet\to F$ satisfying the strict equations
$$\ell(i\times1)=a(1\times v),\qquad f\ell=b(1\times v).$$
Products with simplicial sets are computed objectwise. All hypercover matching objects and refinement morphisms are formed in presheaves.

source.place: Dugger--Hollander--Isaksen, Hypercovers and simplicial presheaves, arXiv:math/0205027v2, Proposition 5.1 (diagram (5.2), conclusion (5.3)) and proof via Proposition 5.5, printed pp. 13-14; specialized to objectwise Kan F,G. Local acyclic fibrations are defined in Section 3, pp. 6-8. Read online; archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this arbitrary-site simplicial-presheaf lifting theorem.
